topic: Typhoon development, structure, and Philippine impacts
key_concepts: Typhoons, hurricanes, and cyclones are the same weather phenomenon named by location
Typhoon categories are based on wind speed
A tropical cyclone has an eye, eyewall, and rain bands
The eye is calm, mostly cloud-free, and has the lowest air pressure
The eyewall has the strongest winds and heaviest rain
Rain bands produce heavy bursts of rain and wind
Typhoon formation requires warm ocean water, humidity, instability, Coriolis effect, and l
The Philippines uses 'bagyo' for all tropical cyclone categories
The Northwestern Pacific Basin is the most active tropical cyclone basin
Typhoons commonly make landfall in Eastern Visayas, Bicol, and northern Luzon
PAGASA monitors tropical cyclones and issues wind signal warnings
Tropical cyclone wind signals correspond to wind speed and lead time
